homepage_intro: Find a map from a IIIF-enabled map collection, copy its IIIF URL and paste it below to start georeferencing. You can view georeferenced maps in Allmaps Viewer or use them in tools like MapLibre, OpenLayers, Leaflet or QGIS.
homepage_pick_collection: Or pick a map from these collections
open_iiif_resource_from_url: Open a IIIF resource from a URL
search_or_paste_iiif_url: Search for something or paste a IIIF URL…
copy_georeference_annotation_url: Copy Georeference Annotation URL to clipboard
copy_viewer_url: Copy Allmaps Viewer URL to clipboard
tour_workflow_description: Georeferencing with Allmaps Editor consists of four steps: selecting an image, drawing a mask, adding control points, and reviewing the result. All edits are saved automatically.
tour_source_title: You’re currently georeferencing this IIIF resource
tour_source_description: IIIF is an open standard that libraries, archives, and museums use to share digitized material and its metadata. Every IIIF resource is published at a URL. To georeference an image with Allmaps Editor, you need to know its IIIF URL.
tour_info_description: Open this panel to see the URL and metadata of the currently loaded IIIF resource.
tour_images_description: Select the image you want to georeference.
tour_mask_description: A mask defines the area of the image that contains the map. An image can contain several maps, such as inset maps or separate map frames. Each map can have its own mask and control points.
tour_search_description: Search for a modern or historical place name to find the right area on the modern map before adding GCPs.
tour_georeference_description: Add a ground control point (GCP) by clicking the same recognizable location on the digitized map on the left and the modern map on the right. Spread control points across the map. To rotate either map, hold Ctrl and drag with the left mouse button.
tour_map_settings_description: Use these settings to adjust the warped map’s opacity, show or hide masks, choose a background map, and display other georeferenced maps in the background.
tour_maps_description: The Maps panel shows the maps and their GCPs. Select a map to view its points and settings. Use the delete button beside a GCP to delete that point, or the delete button beside a map to delete the entire map.
tour_maps_empty_description: This image has no maps yet. Draw a mask or add GCPs to create one. You can then manage its GCPs here, including deleting individual points.
tour_maps_incomplete_description: This image has a map, but it needs at least two complete GCPs before Allmaps can show a georeferenced result.
tour_maps_multiple_description: Each map can have its own mask, GCPs, transformation, and projection. This is useful for inset maps or images with several separate map frames.
tour_map_row_description: A row represents one map area in the image. Use the thumbnail to recognize the mask and switch between maps.
tour_transformation_description: The transformation controls how GCPs warp the digitized map and how pixel coordinates are converted into geographic coordinates. The projection tells Allmaps which coordinate reference system was used for the digitized map, helping warp it more accurately with fewer GCPs.
tour_gcps_description: A GCP links a point on the digitized map to the same location on the modern map. Spread GCPs across the map to improve the result. For geographically accurate maps, 3–10 GCPs are usually enough. Older or less accurate maps may need more.
tour_results_description: Use Results to check how the digitized map aligns with the modern map.
tour_results_pending_description: Once a map in the current image has enough GCPs, you can check how it aligns with the modern map here.
tour_export_description: All edits are saved automatically. Use this panel to open your map in Allmaps Viewer, share a link, or use the georeferencing data and map tiles in other applications.
tour_export_pending_description: All edits are saved automatically. Once a map has enough GCPs, this panel provides links to view, share, and use the georeferenced map in other applications.
export_geojson_description: Export the mask of current map view as a GeoJSON file.
geotiff_description: It's possible to turn Georeference Annotations into GeoTIFFs. To do this, you need to install GDAL. Install Allmaps CLI.
autosave_notice: All edits are automatically saved in the Allmaps database
no_images_georeferenced: No images have been georeferenced. Select an image and start by drawing a mask or by placing ground control points (GCPs)
image_not_georeferenced: This image has not yet been georeferenced. Start by drawing a mask or by placing ground control points (GCPs)

edit_gcps_description: Edit the GCPs of the current map in the text field below.
edit_gcps_formats: You can use the formats used by QGIS, GDAL and ESRI. You can use the Upload button to read the GCPs from a file on your computer.
edit_mask_description: Edit the mask of the current map in the text field below. Supported formats:
plain_text_coordinate_pairs: Plain text list of coordinate pairs, one per line, e.g.
json_coordinate_pairs: JSON array of coordinate pairs, e.g.
current_image_dimensions: The dimensions of the current image are {width} x {height} pixels
line_two_parts_error: Line does not have two parts: {pair}
invalid_resource_mask_array: Resource mask is not a valid array of points
coordinate_line_format_error: Each line should be of the form "x,y" where x and y are numbers
resource_mask_minimum_points: Resource mask should have at least 3 points
invalid_json_error: The server did not return valid JSON.
invalid_json_hint: You might have used the URL of an HTML web page instead of a IIIF resource, or the IIIF resource is invalid.
status_code_error: The server returned a {status} status code.
unauthorized_error: You're not authorized to access this resource. Allmaps Editor can only access IIIF resources that are publicly available.
cors_error: The IIIF resource you are trying to load may be blocked by a missing or invalid CORS policy.
cors_hint: You can try to open the JSON contents of the IIIF resource in a new tab. If your browser can correctly display its contents, this probably means that the IIIF server does not send the correct CORS headers. To fix this, contact the institution that manages the IIIF server and ask them to enable CORS.
invalid_url_error: The IIIF URL you are trying to load is invalid.
invalid_protocol_error: Allmaps Editor can only load IIIF resources over HTTPS. Because Allmaps Editor itself is loaded from a secure HTTPS origin, browsers disallow loading resources from insecure origins.
mixed_content_link: disallows loading resources from insecure origins
invalid_domain_error: The resource domain cannot be accessed: {domain}
parse_iiif_error: Allmaps Editor couldn't parse the IIIF resource you're trying to load. This probably means that the IIIF resource is incorrect but it could also mean that the Allmaps IIIF parser needs to be improved. You can use the IIIF Presentation API Validator to see if the IIIF resource contains errors.
